description.narrative:
Insatsen övergripande mål:
1. "Contribute to reduce the most pressing needs of children affected by the Venezuelan socio-economic and political crisis in Venezuela".
Insatsens specifika mål:
2. "Increased access to integrated multi-sectoral education and protection services for the children most affected by the Venezuelan socio-economic and political crisis Venezuela".

Rädda Barnen (Save the Children Sweden) has applied to Sida for funding of 1 452 810 SEK to carry out the EU-project "Multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance to vulnerable children and their families affected by the crisis in Venezuela" during 2020-2021.
The project's overall objective:
1. "Contribute to reduce the most pressing needs of children affected by the Venezuelan socio-economic and political crisis in Venezuela"
The project's specific objective:
2. "Increased access to integrated multi-sectoral education and protection services for the children most affected by the Venezuelan socio-economic and political crisis Venezuela"
Rädda Barnen will collaborate with local civil society organisations "Fe y Alegria" (F&A) and "Fundación Amigos del Niño que Amerita Protección" (FUNDANA). Rädda Barnen has the overall responsibility for the coordination and implementation of the project.
The contribution has the EU Commission reference number ECHO/-AM/BUD/2020/91040. The contribution's total budget is 1 540 000 EUR, which corresponds to approximately 15 616 597 SEK. The requested support from Sida is 1 452 810 SEK, which corresponds to 10 percent of the total budget.

Rädda Barnen har ansökt om finansiering av egeninsats om 1 452 810 SEK för EU-projektet "Multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance to vulnerable children and their families affected by the crisis in Venezuela" för perioden 2020-2021.
Insatsen övergripande mål är att:
1. "Contribute to reduce the most pressing needs of children affected by the Venezuelan socio-economic and political crisis in Venezuela"
Insatsens specifika mål:
2. "Increased access to integrated multi-sectoral education and protection services for the children most affected by the Venezuelan socio-economic and political crisis Venezuela"
Rädda Barnen kommer att arbeta i samverkan med de lokala civilsamhällesorganisationerna "Fe y Alegria" (F&A) och "Fundación Amigos del Niño que Amerita Protección" (FUNDANA). Rädda Barnen har det övergripande ansvaret för projektets implementering och koordinering.
Den aktuella insatsen har EU-kommissionens referensnummer ECHO/-AM/BUD/2020/91040. Insatsen har en total budget på 1 540 000 EUR, vilket motsvarar cirka 15 616 597 SEK. Av detta har Rädda Barnen beviljats 1 400 000 EUR från EU-kommissionen och ansöker om 1 452 810 SEK (cirka 10 procent) från Sida.

Exempel på uppnådda resultat:
- "The Action accomplished an increasing number of children enrolled and a high permanence during the school year in the 18 Fe y Alegria (FyA) schools. Despite the pandemic context, 8.233 children were enrolled by the end of the Action, reaching 125% of the initial goal (6.584 children). Moreover, the delivery of food kits at schools took place and had a positive impact on the childrens school permanency during the Action. A total of 8.627 people (2.058 girls, 2.143 boys, 2.595 women, and 1.831 men) were reached and according to beneficiaries' testimonials, these kits were a huge help for them".
- "To strengthen local capacities, the Action included a comprehensive capacity building package for the two partners involved, Fe y Alegría (FyA) and FUNDANA. Both organisations conducted training workshops for their teams, consisting of 91 staff (81 female and 10 male). These workshops included three thematic areas: (1) organizational strengthening, (2) humanitarian principles, and (3) technical or programmatic capacities. Organizational strengthening included training on financial issues, supply chain, fraud, and corruption. Humanitarian assistance included humanitarian principles, data protection, policies against sexual exploitation and abuse, and safeguarding. In terms of technical or programmatic capacities, training was provided on inclusion policies, gender equality, accountability, monitoring, and evaluation systems, thus ensuring the collection of reliable information".
- "Another way to strengthen Civil Society was through the work developed with local communities including children's participation. During the Action, 17 community protection committees were created, with a total of 137 volunteers nationwide (115 female and 22 male). Committee members strengthened their knowledge of duties and rights of both adult citizens and children. Members were taught about state institutions, about their capacities to use effective conflict resolution mechanisms, making them less dependent on organizations that do not provide solutions or are not sustainable. These community protection committees received more than 30 trainings on case identification and referral, referral routes, community protection mechanisms, child protection issues, including data protection, and positive parenting inclusion".
